text:
Alex: Heads-up — rapid release planned for Tue (EoQ push + partner promo). Need a fast capacity check for GPU pools, especially eu-west and us-west. Who can eyeball GPU hours and overflow plan? :rotating_light:
Meera: I can run the projection. Do we have expected QPS/avg tokens per request for the promo?
Jon: Promo page says ~10k concurrent users for 15m bursts, median prompt ~80 tokens, generation avg 120 tokens. I'll drop numbers to you.
Meera: OK running quick calc: 10k conc * 15m burst -> 150k user-minutes. With avg response ~0.22s per token on p3x -> approx 4.4M token-seconds -> ~1.22 GPU-hours per second? Wait hold on, roughing it: I get ~85 GPU-hours for the 15m burst if we don't batch aggressively. Need better perf profile. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Alex: Can we leverage Dedicated reserved pools + some spot? Cost tradeoffs?
Jon: We have 120 reserved GPU-hours available in eu-west this week. We can buy short-term burst pool from cloud partner for the promo window. Spot in eu-west is flaky during peak retail times.
Laura: Also watch C-level egress — partner assets will be fetched from S3 in us-west causing cross-region egress if not cached. Recommend pre-warming CDN edge and using signed URLs in eu-west to avoid cross-region traffic.
Ryan: Cost quick note — if we use on-demand instead of reserved for the extra 100 GPU-hours, estimate +35% cost. If we buy a 1-day reserved, about +10%. We should run exact numbers against billing API.
Amanda: Ops checklist: 1) Increase autoscale max for model-serving pool to +40% for the promo window. 2) Pre-warm caches (embedding + prefix KV) 3) Canary traffic at 5% for first 10m then 20% next 10m.
infra-bot: Scheduled job created: autoscale-policy-update(applied) target_pool=nlp-prod-max_increase=40% window=2026-11-02T14:00:00Z-2026-11-02T16:30:00Z
Meera: I ran a forecast using recent traffic patterns and current batching efficiency. Results: baseline 24h expected GPU-hours 480, promo spike adds ~95-110 GPU-hours (95 optimistic w/ autoscale & prefix caching, 110 pessimistic). Attaching quick numbers inline:
```
scenario,extra_gpu_hours
optimistic,95
nominal,103
pessimistic,110
```
Jon: Recommended mitigation: enable forced smaller batching window (50ms) during surge to reduce tail latency, and enable KV prefix caching for identical prompts from partner. Also prepare model fallback plan: if eu-west capacity < 80% we failover to us-west at longer latency but lower cost per token.
Alex: Network concern from Laura noted — Amanda, can ops validate CDN pre-warm by EOD?
Amanda: Yes. I'll run a small synthetic run to warm the bucket + run curl checks from eu-west nodes. Will post results.
Laura: Also let's add an ingress rate-limit for partner route to protect backend if partner bot misbehaves. 200r/s per key, with burst 500.
Ryan: Fine. I'll put 2 cost scenarios in the ticket: (A) reserved + short burst pool, (B) pure on-demand. Tagging finance for quick approval.
Meera: One more: we should pin model version for the release window (no auto-rollouts). I'll set rollout policy to manual between 13:30-16:30 UTC.
Jon: Ops action for drain/scale if needed (snippet):
```
# drain low-priority nodes
kubectl cordon node-gpu-12
kubectl drain node-gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
# bump deployment
kubectl patch deploy model-serving --patch '{"spec":{"replicas":60}}'
```
Alex: Good. Can we have a short runbook in case eu-west hits 90%? Steps + contacts?
Amanda: I'll author a 1-pager and post to #runbooks by EOD. Will include rollback, fallback to us-west, and cost kill-switch (auto-scale down to baseline).
Meera: I'll update forecast numbers in the ticket with 95/103/110 and include GPU-hour burn-rate graphs.
Alex: Thanks all. Final ask: tag on-call, set incident threshold: gpu_util > 90% for 5m -> page SRE. Everyone ok? :thumbsup:
Jon: ok
Laura: ok
Ryan: ok
Amanda: ok
Meera: ok
Alex: Great — we'll reconvene 1h before launch for quick green/red check.
